lines.text: Lagos has two names. And both stories start somewhere else.
In the fourteen hundreds, Portuguese sailors reached the coast and named it Lagos, which means lakes, after its lagoons.
But the city already had an older name: Eko.
Many historians link Eko to the Benin Kingdom, whose soldiers kept a war camp there. In the Benin language, Eko is said to mean war camp.
Today, Lagos calls itself the Centre of Excellence. But locals still say: Eko o ni baje. Lagos will not spoil!
